name: Bangolan
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: Njeck, Mathaus 2003. Phonological sketch of Bangolan (NACALCO, Yaounde); also Njeck 2003b, A Phonology of Bangulan and a Proposed Orthography (Maitrise thesis, Univ. of Yaounde I)
earlier_scan.note: Grassfields Bantu with 3 level + 3 contour lexical tones per Wikipedia; phonological sketch exists but PDF not locatable online

sources.citation: Njeck 2003 thesis, section 1.5 Review of literature (p. 8), naming Grimes 1992 (Ethnologue), Nashipu 1989 (dialectometrical study of the Ndop plain languages), Graffin 1994 (SIL rapid appraisal survey of Bangolan) and Ndiwane 2000 (history)
sources.note: The thesis states these earlier works 'are mainly concerned with the classification of Băŋgulaŋ. There is none that has done a descriptive work on the language' (p. 8); none is a phonological description.

sources.citation: Mbah, Njeck Mathaus. 2003. A phonology of Băŋgulaŋ and a proposed orthography. Maîtrise dissertation, Department of African Languages and Linguistics, University of Yaoundé I (Dec. 2003), x+91 pp. (supervisors Tamanji Pius, Ndamsah Gratiana).
sources.access_detail: copy on file; access check: not located online or in the libraries checked
sources.note: Nothing: no occurrence of stress/accent/prominence/intonation anywhere in the scanned text layer (checked with scanned-variant spellings). Chapter 4 'Tones' (pp. 46-59) describes a tone language with three level tones (H, M, L) and three contour tones (LH rising, HL falling, plus a low-falling tone), lexical minimal pairs and grammatical tone (imperative H vs progressive M on verbs); ch. 5 word structure (pp. 60-69) gives syllable/word templates with no prominence marks; ch. 6 orthography marks tone only. 'BZggularJ [Băŋgulaŋ] has no dialect' (p. 7).

sources.citation: Njeck, Mathaus [Mbah]. 2003. Phonological sketch of Bangolan. Yaoundé: NACALCO (BASAL project), November 2003, 19 pp. SIL Language & Culture Archives record 47360.
sources.note: Nothing: no stress/accent/prominence/intonation terms; 'prosodies' refers only to Firthian labialisation/palatalisation/prenasalisation. Section 5 'Tone' (pp. 16-18): 'We have identified five basic phonetic pitches on single syllables in Bangolan: three level tones, high, mid, and low; and three contour tones, low-high rising, high-low falling and low-falling' (p. 16; tone-letter diacritics garbled in the text layer), lexical minimal pairs (pp. 16-17), contrast chart (p. 18), one grammatical-tone contrast 'he has gone' vs 'he is going' (p. 18).

sources.citation: Wikipedia, 'Bangolan language' (accessed 2026-09-17), Tone section citing Njeck 2003a pp. 16-18
sources.note: Nothing on stress; reports 3 level + 3 contour tones, lexical and grammatical tone, all second-hand from the NACALCO sketch.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.1 languoid record bang1356 (JSON) and PHOIBLE 2.0 inventory PH 1183 (Bangolan, 40 segments)
sources.note: Bibliographic only: Glottolog's most extensive descriptions are Njeck 2003 (phonology) and Koelle 1854 (wordlist); PHOIBLE lists segments only, nothing on stress.
